determination_table_content.details:
Partnered Health Medical Centres Pty Ltd (Partnered Health)’s
proposed acquisition of Ryan Plaza Medical Services Pty Ltd (Ryan
Plaza) (together, the Parties) (the Acquisition).

The Australian Competition and Consumer Commission has
determined under section 51ABZE(1) of the Competition and
Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) that the Acquisition may be put into effect.

The acquirer, Partnered Health, is part of the Partnered Health Group
and an indirectly wholly-owned subsidiary of Partnered Health Pty
Ltd (PHPL). PHPL is part of a larger group of companies which are
majority owned by Quadrant Private Equity (QPE) through Quadrant
Private Equity No. 6 (QPE Fund 6).
Partnered Health together with other PHPL subsidiaries (PH Primary
Care Group) provide primary care services through 67 general
practice clinics and medical centres across Australia, engaging
approximately 570 general practitioners. The PH Primary Care Group
also operates skin cancer clinics, allied health providers
(physiotherapy and dietetics) and TeleWell, a 24/7 telehealth
platform.
The target, Ryan Plaza, operates a single medical centre called
“Medicine on Second” at Maroochydore, Queensland. Ryan Plaza
provides primary care services through 11 general practitioners.

The parties overlap in the supply of primary care (general medical)
services in the Maroochydore region, Queensland.

When making a determination in Phase 1, the Australian Competition
and Consumer Commission (ACCC) undertakes a competition
assessment and considers whether it is appropriate for an
acquisition to be approved or subject to further assessment in
Phase 2 in accordance with section 51ABZJ of the Competition and
Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act). In doing so, the ACCC must have
regard to the object of the Act and all relevant matters, including the
interests of consumers.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notified acquisitions, see the ACCC’s merger assessment guidelines
and interim merger process guidelines.
In conducting its competition assessment, the ACCC has considered
the information and documents that were submitted with the
notification form and publicly available information.
The ACCC has determined that the Acquisition may be put into
effect as it considers that the Acquisition is unlikely to have the
effect of substantially lessening competition in any market. In
reaching its decision, and based on the material before it, the ACCC
makes the following findings.
• The market share aggregation arising from the Acquisition
appears low.
• The Parties would likely continue to face competition from
alternative suppliers of primary care (general medical) services
in the Maroochydore region, Queensland.

A notifying party, or other person who has been allowed to do so by
the Australian Competition Tribunal, may apply for review if they are
dissatisfied with the determination. Pursuant to section 100C of the
Act, applications for review of the determination are to be made to
the Australian Competition Tribunal before the end of 14 calendar
days after this statement of reasons was included on the ACCC’s
Acquisitions Register. To confirm whether there has been any
application for review, please contact the Australian Competition
Tribunal.

determination_table_content.details:
AP Emerald (Luxembourg) S.à r.l. (AP Emerald) and Apollo Capital
Management, L.P. applied for a notification waiver in respect of the
proposed acquisition by AP Emerald of 46% of the share capital and
voting rights of Bayer Asset Management B.V. from Bayer Global
Investments B.V., as described in the transaction documents
provided as part of the application (the Acquisition).
Bayer Global Investments B.V. will retain a majority share in Bayer
Asset Management B.V. At closing of the Acquisition, Bayer Asset
Management B.V. will indirectly hold 100% of the shares in Bayer Oy.

The Australian Competition and Consumer Commission has
determined under section 51ABV(1)(a) of the Competition and
Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.
8 August 2026

AP Emerald is a special purpose vehicle which is indirectly managed
and advised by affiliates of Apollo Capital Management, L.P., a
wholly-owned indirect subsidiary of Apollo Global Management, Inc.
(together with its indirect subsidiaries managing the investment
fund, Apollo). Apollo is a global alternative asset manager
headquartered in New York.
Bayer Asset Management B.V. is a newly incorporated entity wholly
owned by Bayer Global Investments B.V. with the sole purpose of
indirectly holding all shares in Bayer Oy. Bayer Asset Management
B.V. is ultimately controlled by Bayer Aktiengesellschaft (together
with its subsidiaries, Bayer). Bayer is a globally active life science
company with its headquarters in Leverkusen, Germany. Bayer
conducts its business in three divisions: pharmaceuticals, consumer
health and crop science. Bayer Oy, which is headquartered in Turku,
Finland, produces long-acting reversible contraceptives.

In making this notification waiver determination, the Australian
Competition and Consumer Commission (the ACCC) has considered
the information provided with the notification waiver application and
certain publicly available information, and had regard to the factors
in section 51ABV(2)(b) of the Competition and Consumer Act 2010
(Cth) (the Act).
Based on the information currently before it, the ACCC considers that
the Acquisition is unlikely to give rise to any material lessening of
competition given:
a. there is no horizontal overlap between Apollo (and its
connected entities) and Bayer Oy in the supply of long-acting
reversible contraceptives
b. there is a low risk of foreclosure or other concerning vertical
or conglomerate effects resulting from exclusionary
conduct, bundling or tying of products or services post-
acquisition.
In these circumstances, the ACCC does not consider it necessary to
reach a concluded view on the likelihood of the notification
thresholds being met.
Given that material competition concerns are unlikely to arise, the
ACCC has determined that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.
The ACCC considers that the determination is consistent with the
object of the Act and the interests of consumers in promoting
competition.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notification waiver applications and to assessing competition
effects more generally, see the ACCC’s guidance on notification
waivers and merger assessment guidelines.

determination_table_content.details:
The proposed joint venture combines Analogic Corporation
(Analogic) with the assets and entities that comprise Leidos, Inc.
(Leidos)’s Security Enterprise Solutions and Industrial and General
Automation businesses (Leidos SES) (the Acquisition).

The Australian Competition and Consumer Commission has
determined under section 51ABZE(1) of the Competition and
Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) that the Acquisition may be put into effect.

Analogic, controlled by affiliates of Altaris Partners LLC (Altaris) is a
US-based company focussed on the healthcare, industrial and
aviation security sectors. It is active in the design, development,
manufacturing and support of advanced imaging and detection
solutions, as well as power and automation systems. Analogic is
active in aviation security globally and supplies explosive detection
systems, including components of checked baggage explosive
detection systems, to original equipment manufacturers overseas,
which may then be supplied into Australia.
Altaris is an investment firm focussed on acquiring and building
companies in the healthcare sector. It has invested in more than 50
companies across a range of healthcare subsectors.
Leidos is a US-based industry and technology company serving
government and commercial customers under the Intelligence &
Digital, Health, Homeland and Defense groupings. Leidos SES is
active in aviation security globally and supplies cabin and checked
baggage explosive detection systems in Australia.

determination_table_content.item:
Overlap and relationship
between the Parties
determination_table_content.details:
Globally, Analogic and Leidos (the Parties) overlap in the supply of
cabin and checked baggage explosive detection systems.
In Australia, Leidos competes to supply explosive detection systems
directly to airport customers. Analogic supplies goods and services,
including explosive detection equipment, service parts, engineering
services and/or systems related to its cabin and checked baggage
products, to other equipment manufacturers, which may then be
supplied to Australian customers.
Checked baggage explosive detection systems are used in airports
for the screening of baggage that has been checked in by
passengers to be stored in the hold of the aircraft. Cabin baggage
explosive detection systems are used to screen cabin (carry-on)
baggage at airport checkpoints.

When making a determination in Phase 1, the Australian Competition
and Consumer Commission (ACCC) undertakes a competition
assessment and considers whether it is appropriate for an
acquisition to be approved or subject to further assessment in
Phase 2 in accordance with section 51ABZJ of the Competition and
Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act). In doing so, the ACCC must have
regard to the object of the Act and all relevant matters, including the
interests of consumers.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notified acquisitions, see the ACCC’s merger assessment guidelines
and interim merger process guidelines.
In conducting its competition assessment, the ACCC has considered
the information and documents that were submitted with the
notification form, information from third parties and publicly
available information, as relevant.
The ACCC has determined that the Acquisition may be put into
effect as it considers that the Acquisition is unlikely to have the
effect of substantially lessening competition in any market. In
reaching its decision, and based on the material before it, the ACCC
makes the following findings.
• The Parties are not close competitors in the supply of cabin and
checked baggage explosive detection systems to airport
customers in Australia, with Analogic currently having a limited
direct role in supplying Australian airport customers.
• The Parties would continue to face competition from alternative
cabin and checked baggage explosive detection systems
suppliers post-Acquisition, including larger competitors.
• While the merged firm may have the ability and incentive to
engage in a foreclosure strategy, limiting downstream suppliers’
access to for example cabin baggage explosive detection
systems or components, such a strategy is unlikely to
substantially lessen of competition due to the presence of
competing alternative systems and the prospect of new entry.

dissatisfied with the determination. Pursuant to section 100C of the
Act, applications for review of the determination are to be made to
the Australian Competition Tribunal before the end of 14 calendar
days after this statement of reasons was included on the ACCC’s
Acquisitions Register. To confirm whether there has been any
application for review, please contact the Australian Competition
Tribunal.

determination_statement_of_reasons.text: When making a determination in Phase 1, the Australian Competition and Consumer Commission (ACCC) undertakes a competition assessment and considers whether it is appropriate for an acquisition to be approved or subject to further assessment in Phase 2 in accordance with section 51ABZJ of the Competition and Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act). In doing so, the ACCC must have regard to the object of the Act and all relevant matters, including the interests of consumers.

Where the ACCC is satisfied that the acquisition, if put into effect, could, in all the circumstances, have the effect of substantially lessening competition in a market, the ACCC may also consider whether any competition issues can be addressed by one or more conditions.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering notified acquisitions, see the ACCC’s merger assessment guidelines and interim merger process guidelines.
For the reasons given below, the ACCC has determined that the Acquisition may be put into effect, subject to conditions.
Overlap between the parties
Black Rhino and Speedy Cocktails (the Parties) overlap in Roma in:

items: the retail supply of off-premises takeaway liquor
the retail supply of on-premises hospitality services, including dining, gaming, on-premises liquor and/or off-premises takeaway liquor services at pub-style venues
the supply of ancillary function/venue and catering services.

determination_statement_of_reasons.text: The ACCC considers that the merged firm would be likely to continue to face competition from multiple alternative suppliers of ancillary function/venue and catering services in Roma, and has not considered this area of overlap further in these reasons.
Industry background
Retail supply of liquor in Queensland

Within Queensland, the retail supply of on-premises liquor and/or off-premises takeaway liquor is regulated by the Office of Liquor and Gaming Regulation (OLGR).1 Queensland’s liquor licensing regime differs to other states in that only holders of a Commercial Hotel Licence (CHL) may obtain approval from the OLGR to operate a detached bottle shop. Suppliers of off-premises takeaway liquor are therefore limited to commercial hotel licensees.
A CHL authorises the sale of liquor for consumption both on and off the licensed premises during approved opening hours. To qualify for a CHL, a person must meet specific requirements.2

Retail bottle shops typically sell off-premises takeaway liquor as their primary purpose. These bottle shops operate under the authority of a CHL,3 which is associated with a pub/hotel-style venue. Under the applicable liquor licensing framework, the holder of a CHL may operate up to 3 detached bottle shops within a 10-kilometre radius of the licensed pub/hotel premises, subject to compliance with the relevant statutory requirements.4

Retail bottle shops supplying off-premises takeaway liquor may operate under a retail banner group, which provides various services for members, including branding, marketing and promotions, loyalty programs and operational support. Bottlemart and Harry Brown are banner group brands present in Roma, owned by Liquor Marketing Group (LMG), a member-owned retail liquor group. The other banner group brand with a presence in Roma is Cellarbrations, owned by Australian Liquor Marketers (ALM), the liquor wholesale division of Metcash. Although bottle shops may operate under the same retail banners, they may be owned and operated by different businesses.

Banner groups may provide bottle shops with enhanced buying power, promotional programs, recommended retail prices, product range guidelines and marketing support. Based on the information before the ACCC, while these banner group arrangements may include certain requirements for bottle shop operators, they do 1 In Queensland, any business or organisation that sells or supplies alcohol must hold a relevant licence issued by the OLGR. See Liquor and wine licences and permits | Business Queensland. 2 To obtain a CHL, a business must have the principal activity of selling liquor for consumption on the licensed premises, or on and off the premises, together with the provision of meals and accommodation, and premises and catering facilities for people attending a function held on the premises, according to the Liquor Act 1992 (QLD) s 59(1). To meet these criteria, a CHL is only granted to a business that has a commercial kitchen, seats a minimum of 60 patrons, and at least 2 of the following: a dining facility, self-contained accommodation of at least 3 rooms, or a function room facility available for hire (Liquor Act 1992 (QLD) s 61(1)). 3 Liquor Act 1992 (QLD) s 60(1)(d). 4 Liquor Act 1992 (QLD) s 59(3). not materially limit the operators’ ability to determine price and non-price aspects of their offerings, including product range, promotions and opening hours. Further, the ACCC understands that operators of bottle shops can and do switch between banner groups and their associated banner brands.
Retail supply of liquor in Roma

Roma is a regional town in south-west Queensland with an estimated population of 7,1005 and is approximately 5-7 hours’ drive west of Brisbane. Black Rhino entered the retail supply of off-premises takeaway liquor and on-premises hospitality services in Roma in late 2024 through its purchase of Royal on Ninety-Nine and the associated bottle shop, Thirsty Camel (now Bottlemart), which is located at Shop 2, 34-38 Hawthorne Street, Roma (in the Cornetts IGA complex).

There are currently 6 bottle shops in Roma, owned by 3 operators: Black Rhino, Speedy Cocktails, and Australian Venue Co (AVC), as set out in Table 1. 5 Roma, QLD reported a population of 6,838 people in the 2021 Census according to the Australian Bureau of Statistics. Calculated at a 3.7% annual growth rate produces an estimate of 7,090 people in 2026. 3. Competition assessment

The ACCC has considered the effects of the Acquisition by comparing the likely future state of competition if the Acquisition proceeds against the continuation of the current state of competition (being the likely future state of competition if the Acquisition does not proceed).
In reaching its decision, the ACCC has had regard to information provided by the Parties and market participants as well as publicly available information.
Relevant areas of competition
The ACCC considers the relevant areas of competitive overlap for the purposes of its assessment are:

items: the retail supply of off-premises takeaway liquor in Roma

the retail supply of on-premises hospitality services, including dining, gaming, on- premises liquor and/or off-premises takeaway liquor services at pub-style venues in Roma. Retail supply of off-premises takeaway liquor – bottle shops in Roma

determination_statement_of_reasons.text: The Parties submitted information to the ACCC that indicates they compete closely in relation to the retail supply of off-premises takeaway liquor in Roma via their respective bottle shops.

The ACCC has had regard to information from a range of market participants that indicates that bottle shops compete in local areas on a variety of factors, including prices and promotions, and the perceived quality and range of products and service offered. Feedback also indicates that location (such as being near a supermarket and/or pub) and convenience factors, such as opening hours and ease of vehicle access, also influence purchasing decisions.

The ACCC has examined information regarding both price and non-price factors in assessing how closely the Parties’ bottle shops compete. Information from the Parties demonstrates that Speedy Cocktails’ 2 bottle shops and Black Rhino’s bottle shop provide a range of off-premises takeaway liquor options including beer, wine, pre-mixed drinks, spirits and cider, and that Cellarbrations at Superstore Roma (Speedy Cocktails) stocks a wider range of products than Bottlemart at Cornetts IGA (Black Rhino). The Parties’ data further indicates that their bottle shops have similar top selling products (with some exceptions), and similar pricing at the aggregate level by product category.

Bottlemart at Cornetts IGA (Site 1, Black Rhino) and Northern Road Bottle Shop (Site 3, Speedy Cocktails) both have walk-in pedestrian access (i.e. with no drive through access), while the Cellarbrations at Superstore Roma (Site 2, Speedy Cocktails) has drive-through and pedestrian access. Opening hours range from 10:00am to 7:00- 8:00pm 7 days a week for Northern Road Bottle Shop (Speedy Cocktails) and Bottlemart at Cornetts IGA (Black Rhino), while Cellarbrations at Superstore Roma (Speedy Cocktails) has extended opening hours from 7:00am to 10:00pm-11:30pm 7 days a week.

Consumers typically purchase the bulk of their off-premises takeaway liquor from bottle shops, with information presented to the ACCC, including from market participants, indicating that the sale of off-premises takeaway liquor from pub-style venues or distilleries is not generally considered a close substitute. This is because these other venues do not offer the same breadth of product range or convenience as bottle shops.

The ACCC has concluded that the relevant geographic scope for the retail supply of off-premises takeaway liquor is likely to be limited to Roma. Roma is geographically remote, and bottle shops outside Roma are a significant driving distance away. The ACCC therefore considers that a large proportion of local consumers are unlikely to travel beyond Roma to purchase off-premises takeaway liquor on a regular or frequent basis. Retail supply of on-premises hospitality services – pub-style venues in Roma

The Parties compete in relation to the retail supply of on-premises hospitality services in Roma via their pub-style venues – Royal on Ninety-Nine and Club Hotel Motel Roma. Each pub-style venue provides multiple bar offerings (e.g. a sports bar and public bar), on-premises dining and gaming machines.
Royal on Ninety-Nine operates from 7:00am-12:00am daily, while Club Hotel Motel Roma is open 10:00am-12:00am daily, with discretion to open until 2:00am on Friday and Saturday.

The ACCC has also considered the offerings of several other venues in Roma that provide limited bar services and/or food and/or gaming services, such as the RSL Roma, Roma Turf Club, and Roma Bowls Club. However, the ACCC does not consider that these other venues compete closely with the Parties’ pub style venues in Roma. This is because information provided to the ACCC indicates that these venues in Roma typically have a specific focus, such as supporting veterans or promoting specific sports, which is reflected in their restricted opening hours and limited food and beverage options compared to pubs.
Based on their limited services the ACCC considers that these venues are not a close substitute for consumers seeking access to on-premises hospitality services in Roma.

The ACCC considers that the relevant geographic scope for the supply of on- premises hospitality services is likely to be Roma. The nearest pub-style venue outside Roma is in Wallumbilla, around 40 km from central Roma. The ACCC considers that a large proportion of consumers seeking on-premises hospitality services on a regular basis are unlikely to frequently travel the significantly further distance to pubs outside of Roma.
Competition effects in the retail supply of off-premises takeaway liquor in Roma, QLD

The ACCC is satisfied that, disregarding any conditions the ACCC could include, the Acquisition could, in all the circumstances, have the effect of substantially lessening competition in the retail supply of off-premises takeaway liquor in Roma.

Following the Acquisition, the number of bottle shop operators in Roma would reduce from 3 to 2. AVC would be the only remaining competitor to Black Rhino. The Acquisition would therefore materially increase concentration in an already highly concentrated market.

In addition, the Acquisition could significantly reduce the competitive constraint on Black Rhino. Noting the analysis set out above in paragraphs 3.4 – 3.8, the ACCC considers that Black Rhino’s bottle shop closely competes with Speedy Cocktails’ 2 bottle shops on both price and non-price factors. The Acquisition would therefore remove competition between Black Rhino and Speedy Cocktails, notwithstanding that AVC would continue to compete.

The ACCC considers there is limited likelihood of timely new entry and expansion. Market feedback has indicated that barriers to entry and expansion are likely to be high. This is due to various factors, including the regulatory requirement for a bottle shop to be associated with a CHL, upfront capital investments, potential uncertainty over the timing and level of return in a demand-limited market, and the presence of existing suppliers.

As a result, post-Acquisition, the merged entity could have an increased ability to raise prices and/or reduce the quality and service provided in the retail supply of off- premises takeaway liquor in Roma.

The ACCC considered Black Rhino’s submission regarding the structural characteristics of off-premises takeaway liquor retailing in smaller markets in regional Australia, which questioned whether Roma can economically sustain multiple bottle shop operators. However, as no evidence was put to the ACCC indicating that any existing bottle shop operator in Roma is unviable, the ACCC has not considered this point further.

Having regard to the combination of factors identified in paragraphs 3.15 – 3.19, the ACCC considers, absent any condition, the Acquisition could have the effect of substantially lessening competition in the retail supply of off-premises takeaway liquor products in Roma.
Competition effects in the retail supply of on-premises hospitality services in Roma, QLD
The ACCC considers that the Acquisition is unlikely to have the effect of substantially lessening competition in the retail supply of on-premises hospitality services in Roma.

The ACCC considers the presence of alternative pub-style venues in Roma would likely continue to constrain the merged entity post-Acquisition, such that the merged entity would be unlikely to profitably increase prices and/or reduce the quality of services provided.

Post-Acquisition, in addition to the 2 pub-style venues owned by the merged entity, there would be 3 alternative pub-style venues owned by 2 other entities (set out in Table 2): AVC, which owns the White Bull Tavern and the Commonwealth Hotel, and an independent partnership, which owns the Queens Arms Hotel. All pub-style venues are clustered in a central location (identified in Map 2) with the alternative venues located within walking distance at 120 metres to 850 metres from the Parties’ pub- style venues. The alternative pub-style venues offer similar on-premises hospitality services: dining, gaming, on-premises liquor and/or off-premises takeaway liquor, and opening hours from 10:00am-10:00pm/12:00am daily. Market feedback received by the ACCC indicated the various venues offer a degree of differentiated service levels and quality.

Having regard to the availability of local alternative options and local competitive dynamics, the ACCC considers that the Acquisition is unlikely to have the effect of substantially lessening competition in the retail supply of on-premises hospitality services in Roma. 4. Conditions

The ACCC has determined under s51ABZE(1) of the Act that the Acquisition may be put into effect, subject to the following conditions: a) Black Rhino Group Pty Ltd ACN 609 276 048 and its Related Bodies Corporate (together referred to as Black Rhino) must not put the Acquisition into effect unless the Divestiture Business has been divested to a purchaser approved in writing by the ACCC. b) Black Rhino must provide the ACCC with an executed undertaking under section 87B of the Act in respect of the divestiture of the Divestiture Business, in the form at Attachment A of the determination, within five business days of the date of the determination and comply with that undertaking. (together, the Conditions).

The ACCC must not include conditions unless it is satisfied that, disregarding any conditions the ACCC could include, the Acquisition, if put into effect, could, in all the circumstances, have the effect of substantially lessening competition in any market.

The ACCC must have regard to all relevant matters, and may have regard to the effect on the interests of consumers that compliance with the conditions would have, or be likely to have, or any consumer benefits that would result, or be likely to result from compliance with the conditions.

It is a contravention of section 45AZ of the Act for a person to put the Acquisition into effect and to not comply with any conditions. Where a person does not comply with conditions, the Federal Court may make orders including, in some circumstances, divestiture or a declaration that the acquisition is void.
Assessment with the Conditions

As set out above, the ACCC is satisfied that, disregarding any conditions the ACCC could include, the Acquisition, could, in all the circumstances, have the effect of substantially lessening competition in the retail supply of off-premises takeaway liquor in Roma, Queensland. To address this, the ACCC has decided to include the Conditions in its Determination.
The objective of the Conditions is to address the competition issues identified in respect of the Acquisition, as set out in this determination and statement of reasons.

The Conditions incorporate a remedy offer Black Rhino made to the ACCC on 9 July 2026, with some changes that the ACCC considered appropriate, including to ensure appropriate standard form protections are in place.
The Conditions address the competition issues
The Conditions address the competition issue identified in respect of the supply of off-premises takeaway liquor in Roma detailed above by:

items: preserving an independent supplier and competitive constraint that would otherwise be lost as a result of the Acquisition
facilitating the entry or expansion of an independent competitor through divestiture to a purchaser approved by the ACCC.

determination_statement_of_reasons.text: The ACCC considers the Conditions are effective in addressing the structural change to the market which would otherwise be brought about by the Acquisition, by ensuring that 3 independent bottle shop owners continue to operate in Roma.
The Conditions can be effectively implemented

The ACCC has had regard to whether there are risks associated with implementation of the Conditions that may limit the effectiveness of the Conditions in addressing the competition issues. The ACCC considers the Conditions can be effectively implemented.
Composition of the Divestiture Business

The ACCC considers that the Divestiture Business is appropriately configured and that a suitable purchaser may operate it effectively. The ACCC has had regard to third party feedback in reaching this view as well as the nature and terms of the Conditions and the Undertaking.

In particular, the Divestiture Business is defined expansively in the Undertaking to include all assets, rights, interests and other property associated with the relevant business including what is necessary for the Approved Purchaser to operate the business as a viable, ongoing and effective independent competitor.

The Conditions also require divestiture to an ACCC-approved purchaser before the Acquisition may be put into effect. As such, if the Divestiture Business is not configured to attract an appropriate purchaser, or cannot be separated for divestiture, the Acquisition will not proceed, and the competition issues from the Acquisition will not arise.
Emergence of appropriate purchaser

Based on submissions provided by the Parties and third party feedback, the ACCC considers an appropriate purchaser can emerge to support a timely and effective divestiture to an ACCC-approved purchaser. The ACCC will consider the materials provided to it in a Proposed Purchaser Notice and may have regard to the factors set out in clause 6.5 of the Undertaking.

As set out at 2.7 – 2.9 above, suppliers of off-premises takeaway liquor in Queensland are limited to commercial hotel licensees, who in turn are limited to operating up to 3 detached bottle shops that must be within a 10-kilometre radius of the licensed pub/hotel premises (and subject to compliance with relevant statutory requirements). The ACCC has had regard to this in assessing the likelihood of an appropriate purchaser emerging, noting this may limit potential purchasers available for the Divestiture Business.

The ACCC notes that the Conditions require divestiture to an ACCC-approved purchaser before the Acquisition may be put into effect. As such, if an appropriate purchaser does not emerge, the Acquisition will not proceed, and the competition issues from the Acquisition will not arise.
Integrity of Divestiture Business and other considerations

The ACCC considers that the integrity of the Divestiture Business will be protected prior to divestiture, and took into account other considerations related to the effective implementation of the Conditions.
The ACCC considers that the risk to the integrity of the Divestiture Business is appropriately managed in the circumstances, including because:

items: the Undertaking includes Divestiture Business Protection obligations on Black Rhino

the Conditions and the Undertaking provide that the Acquisition may only complete once the Divestiture Business has been divested to an ACCC-approved purchaser, which the ACCC considers also incentivises Black Rhino to ensure the business is appropriately managed and maintained prior to divestiture, including so that it is attractive to purchasers.

determination_statement_of_reasons.text: The ACCC also considers that any risk that divestiture will be frustrated, for example, due to third-party consents and renewals is appropriately managed by the terms of the Undertaking, and because divestiture of the Divestiture Business must occur before the Acquisition can complete.

The ACCC notes that performance of certain obligations in the Undertaking requires Black Rhino to procure that Speedy Cocktails performs the obligation, who is not a party to the Undertaking. The ACCC considers this is unlikely to impact the effective implementation of the conditions noting that Black Rhino must not complete the Acquisition unless divestiture occurs. 5. determination_table_content.details:
Foxtrott BidCo GmbH, indirectly controlled by the Triton Fund 6 GP
SARL (Triton) applied for a notification waiver in respect of its
proposed acquisition of 100% of the issued share capital of Flender
Group GmbH (Flender), as described in the transaction documents
provided as part of the application (the Acquisition).

The Australian Competition and Consumer Commission has
determined under section 51ABV(1)(a) of the Competition and
Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.
11 August 2026

The acquirer, Foxtrott BidCo GmbH, is indirectly controlled by Triton
Fund 6 GP SARL in its capacity as general partner of Triton Fund 6
SCSp, which together with a number of other limited partnerships,
form part of Triton Fund 6, a private equity fund. Triton Fund 6 is one
of the investments funds (the Triton Funds) managed and advised
by entities being part of the Triton group.
The Triton Funds, including Triton Fund 6, invest in medium sized
companies headquartered in Central and Northern Europe operating
in different markets, with particular focus on three core sectors:
Business Services, Industrial Tech and Healthcare. In addition to
managing private equity investment funds (Triton Fund I, IA, II, III, IV,
V, and 6) and related activities and investments in middle-market
companies (through the Triton Smaller Mid-Cap Funds), Triton also
invests in credit facilities (through the Triton Debt Opportunities
Funds).
Relevant to the Acquisition, Triton Funds controls a portfolio
company active in the wind turbine sector, FairWind, which provides
wind turbine installation and lifecycle support.
The target, Flender, is a German company engaged in the
manufacture and supply of mechanical drive products and
generators for industrial applications, power generation and the wind
power industry, together with associated maintenance and repair
services.
In Australia, Flender operates through its subsidiary Flender Pty Ltd,
and supplies services related to wind turbine drivetrain components,
as well as supplying and servicing gearboxes and couplings for
industrial applications such as mining. Flender does not carry out
any manufacturing activities in Australia, and does not supply wind
turbine drivetrain components (including gearboxes, couplings and
generators) in Australia.

In making this notification waiver determination, the Australian
Competition and Consumer Commission (the ACCC) has considered
the information provided with the notification waiver application and
had regard to the factors in section 51ABV(2)(b) of the Competition
and Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act).
Based on the information provided in the application, the ACCC
considers that the Acquisition is unlikely to give rise to any material
lessening of competition given:
a. there is no horizontal overlap between Triton and Flender in
the supply of wind turbine installation and lifecycle services,
or specialised repair and servicing of wind turbine gearboxes
and generators
b. there is a low risk of foreclosure or other concerning vertical
or conglomerate effects resulting from exclusionary
conduct, bundling or tying of products or services post-
acquisition
c. the presence of alternative suppliers of wind turbine
installation and lifecycle services, and specialised repair and
servicing of wind turbine gearboxes and generators in
Australia.
In these circumstances, the ACCC does not consider it necessary to
reach a concluded view on the likelihood of the notification
thresholds being met.
Given that material competition concerns are unlikely to arise, the
ACCC has determined that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.
The ACCC considers that the determination is consistent with the
object of the Act and the interests of consumers in promoting
competition.

notification waiver applications and to assessing competition
effects more generally, see the ACCC’s guidance on notification
waivers and merger assessment guidelines.

determination_table_content.details:
Siemens Mobility Holding B.V. (Siemens Mobility Holding) proposes
to acquire 100% of the share capital of MerMec S.p.A. (MerMec) (the
Acquisition) from its holding company, Angelo Holding S.r.l (Angelo
Holding).1

The Australian Competition and Consumer Commission has
determined under section 51ABZE(1) of the Competition and
Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) that the Acquisition may be put into effect.

The acquirer, Siemens Mobility Holding, is an investment vehicle and
wholly owned subsidiary of Siemens Aktiengesellschaft (Siemens
AG), a German stock corporation with registered seats in Berlin and
Munich (Germany) and headquartered in Munich. Siemens AG is the
ultimate parent of the Siemens group of companies (Siemens). The
Acquisition is being led by Siemens AG’s wholly controlled
subsidiary and mobility business, Siemens Mobility GmbH. Unless
otherwise specified, Siemens Mobility Holding and Siemens Mobility
GmbH are together referred to as SMO.
SMO operates in Australia through its subsidiary, Siemens Mobility
Pty Ltd, and supplies:
• signalling systems (technology to control railway traffic)
• rolling stock (wheeled vehicles used on railway systems)
• rolling stock diagnostics (technology used to monitor the
condition of rolling stock)
• rail infrastructure diagnostics (technology to detect defects on
rail infrastructure, such as railway lines), to a limited historical
extent.
The target, MerMec, is an Italian company headquartered in
Monopoli, Italy. It is wholly owned by Angelo Holding. MerMec
operates in Australia through its subsidiary, MerMec Australia Pty
Ltd and in Australia supplies rail infrastructure diagnostics, rolling
stock diagnostics, and products used in steel and industrial
manufacturing quality control.
MerMec and SMO are together referred to as the Parties.

In Australia, the Parties overlap in the supply of rolling stock
diagnostics and rail infrastructure diagnostics. MerMec’s rail
infrastructure diagnostic components can also be installed on rolling
stock and supplied with SMO’s rolling stock.

When making a determination in Phase 1, the Australian Competition
and Consumer Commission (ACCC) undertakes a competition
assessment and considers whether it is appropriate for an
acquisition to be approved or subject to further assessment in
Phase 2 in accordance with section 51ABZJ of the Competition and
Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act). In doing so, the ACCC must have
regard to the object of the Act and all relevant matters, including the
interests of consumers.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notified acquisitions, see the ACCC’s merger assessment guidelines
and interim merger process guidelines.
In conducting its competition assessment, the ACCC has considered
the information and documents that were submitted with the
notification form, information from third partes, and publicly
available information.
The ACCC has determined that the Acquisition may be put into
effect as it considers that the Acquisition is unlikely to have the
effect of substantially lessening competition in any market. In
reaching its decision, and based on the material before it, the ACCC
makes the following findings.
• The Parties are not close competitors in the supply of rolling
stock diagnostics or rail infrastructure diagnostics.
• The merged firm would continue to face competition from
multiple alternative suppliers of rolling stock diagnostics and rail
infrastructure diagnostics in Australia.
• The merged firm would be unlikely to have the ability and
incentive to foreclose rival suppliers of rolling stock by denying
or limiting their access to rail infrastructure diagnostics
components, given there are multiple alternative suppliers of
such components in Australia.
• The merged firm would be unlikely to have the ability and
incentive to foreclose rival suppliers of rail infrastructure
diagnostics by denying or limiting their access to customers of
those components by limiting installation on the merged entity’s
rolling stock, given rolling stock OEMs are not significant
purchasers of these components and there are multiple
alternative acquirers of such components in Australia.

A notifying party, or other person who has been allowed to do so by
the Australian Competition Tribunal, may apply for review if they are
dissatisfied with the determination. Pursuant to section 100C of the
Act, applications for review of the determination are to be made to
the Australian Competition Tribunal before the end of 14 calendar
days after this statement of reasons was included on the ACCC’s
Acquisitions Register. To confirm whether there has been any
application for review, please contact the Australian Competition
Tribunal.

When making a determination in Phase 1, the Australian Competition
and Consumer Commission (ACCC) undertakes a competition
assessment and considers whether it is appropriate for an
acquisition to be approved or subject to further assessment in
Phase 2 in accordance with section 51ABZJ of the Competition and

consolidation in the relevant market and make it difficult for

determination_table_content.details:
Expedia Group, Inc. (Expedia) proposes to acquire the entire issued
share capital of Ballast Group Holdings Ltd (trading as CarTrawler)
(the Acquisition).

The Australian Competition and Consumer Commission has
determined under section 51ABZE(1) of the Competition and
Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) that the Acquisition may be put into effect.

Expedia operates online travel agency brands, including
Expedia.com, Hotels.com, and Vrbo, and is the majority owner of
Trivago, which is principally a hotel meta-search site. Expedia is
primarily active in the supply of online booking intermediation
services on a standalone and package basis for hotel rooms, flights,
car rental, activities and experiences, cruises and alternative
accommodations to consumers.
In addition to its consumer-facing (B2C) operations, Expedia also
provides business-to business (B2B) intermediation distribution
solutions, which enable a wide range of travel and non-travel
partners (including airlines, offline travel agents, online retailers,
corporate travel management, financial institutions, and other
distributors of travel booking services) to utilise Expedia's
technology to access and distribute travel products, including car
rental services.
CarTrawler is a global provider of distribution solutions for car rental,
ground transportation and travel-related insurance. CarTrawler
primarily offers B2B solutions that enable third-party travel partners,
such as airlines, online travel agencies, tour operators and other
travel distributors, to offer car rental services through their own B2C
customer interfaces. CarTrawler's "Connect" platform is a
proprietary B2B technology platform that supports end to-end
booking, availability and pricing aggregation, payments, and ancillary
travel insurance products. The platform is integrated into partners'
existing booking flows via APIs, allowing CarTrawler’s business
customers (e.g. airlines, online travel agencies, etc.) to offer car
rental products to end consumers.
CarTrawler also operates two B2C brands, Holiday Autos and Angus
Car Hire, which both supply online car rental comparison and
reservation services.

determination_table_content.item:
Overlap and relationship
between the Parties
determination_table_content.details:
Expedia and CarTrawler (together, the Parties) overlap in the supply
of car rental booking services via online intermediated channels,
including in the supply of business-to-business (B2B) and business-
to-consumer (B2C) car rental intermediation distribution solutions.
There is also a non-horizontal relationship between the Parties’
products through CarTrawler’s B2B “Connect” platform being used
as an input into online travel agency services and in conjunction with
a range of other B2B intermediation distribution solutions.

and Consumer Commission (ACCC) undertakes a competition

• There is limited overlap between the Parties in the supply of both

alternative suppliers of car rental intermediation distribution
solutions in Australia.
• The merged entity would be unlikely to have the ability and
incentive to foreclose rival online travel agencies’ access to B2B
car rental intermediation distribution solutions, due to the
availability of alternative suppliers to CarTrawler.
• The merged entity would also be unlikely to have the ability and
incentive to foreclose rival B2B car rental intermediation

Expedia is a leading online travel agency, there are likely

airlines.

management and investment advisory services to several
investment funds. The controlled companies in the Cinven funds’
portfolio of investments are active in a wide range of sectors
including business services, consumer, financial services, healthcare,
industrials and technology, media and telecommunications.
The Cinven funds’ portfolio of investments includes Vitamin Well
Group and Barentz. Vitamin Well Group is a Swedish functional food
and beverage company that develops and sells functional food and
beverages, primarily through its three core brands: Vitamin Well
(vitamin and mineral-enriched drinks), NOCCO (functional drinks)
and Barebells (protein bars and protein drinks). Vitamin Well Group
is not active in the contract manufacturing of functional snack bars
for third-party brands.
Barentz is a Netherlands headquartered company that is a global
specialty ingredients solution provider specialising in human
nutrition, pharmaceuticals, personal care, performance materials and
animal nutrition. Barentz is a supplier and distributor of raw
materials and specialty ingredients.
The target, EMPWR, is a Belgium headquartered company who is
globally active as a developer and contract manufacturer of
functional snack bars, including protein bars, uncoated dough bars,
granola bars, crisp bars, nut bars, and fruit bars at the business-to-
business level for brand-owners and retailers mainly across Europe
and North America. EMPWR co-designs, develops, and manufactures

Netherlands, Canada and the United States.

the information provided with the notification waiver application and

b. there are alternative manufacturers of functional snack bars,

effects resulting from exclusionary conduct in Australia
post-acquisition.
In these circumstances, the ACCC does not consider it necessary to
reach a concluded view on the likelihood of the notification
thresholds being met.
Given that material competition concerns are unlikely to arise, the
